title_short: Penalties for failure or non-compliance in relation to rest days, overtime, holidays, annual leave, and sick leave
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer must pay you for rest day work, overtime work, holiday work, annual leave, and sick leave - if they don't pay, they commit an offence and the court will order them to pay you the wages due.

title_short: Employees on estates to be provided with minimum number of days' work in each mont
legal_title_plain: Minimum work days for estate workers
legal_content_plain_en: If you work on an estate and get paid by days worked, your employer must give you at least 24 days of work each month or still pay you for 24 days.

title_short: Wage period
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer must pay your wages at least once every month.

title_short: Calculation of wages for incomplete month's work
legal_content_plain_en: If you don't work the full month, your pay will be calculated by this formula: (Monthly wages ÷ Days in wage period) * Days you actually worked.

title_short: Time of payment of wages
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer must pay your wages within 7 days after the end of each wage period, and overtime/rest day/holiday wages must be paid by the last day of the next wage period.

title_short: Payment on normal termination of contract
legal_title_plain: Final wage payment on normal termination
legal_content_plain_en: When your contract ends normally, your employer must pay any unpaid wages on the same day your contract ends.

title_short: on breach of contract
legal_title_plain: Final wage payment on immediate termination
legal_content_plain_en: When your contract ends without notice, your employer must pay all wages owed immediately on the termination day.

title_short: Lawful deductions
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer can only make deductions from your wages if allowed by law, and total deductions cannot exceed 50% of your monthly wages.

title_short: Wages to be paid through financial institution
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer must pay your wages through a bank account in your name or an account you choose.

title_short: Payment  of wages  other  than  through  financial institution
legal_content_plain_en: If you request in writing, your employer can pay you with cash or cheque instead of bank transfer, but needs government approval first.

title_short: with whom wages paid to be spent, illegal
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer cannot control where, how, or with whom you spend your wages - any contract rules about this are illegal.

title_short: Interest on advances forbidden
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer cannot charge you interest or fees on wage advances.

title_short: Restriction on places at which wages may be paid
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer cannot pay your wages at bars, entertainment places, or retail shops (unless you work there).

title_short: Hours of work and working at night
legal_title_plain: Daily and weekly working hour limits

title_short: Priority of wages over other debts
legal_content_plain_en: If your employer's property is sold or seized, your unpaid wages must be paid first before other debts.

title_short: Liability of principals and contractors for wages
legal_content_plain_en: If contractors owe you wages, both the main contractor and subcontractor are responsible for paying you.

title_short: Work on rest day
legal_content_plain_en: If you work on rest day: for half day or less, you get normal daily pay; for more than half day, you get 2 days' pay; for overtime on rest day, you get at least 2 times your hourly rate.

title_short: Task  work
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer can agree to pay you based on tasks completed instead of daily or hourly rates.

title_short: Interpretation

title_short: Flexible working arrangement
legal_content_plain_en: You can apply to your employer for flexible working hours, days, or workplace arrangements.

title_short: Employee's remedy when employer about to abscond

title_short: Court order for payments due to employee
legal_content_plain_en: If your employer is convicted of wage violations, the court can order immediate payment to you and can seize their property to pay your wages.

title_short: Duties and responsibilities in respect of safety and health
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer or accommodation provider who provides accommodation must: (a) provide separate accommodation for employees of opposite gender, (b) take necessary preventive measures to ensure employees' safety and well-being, (c) take fire safety measures according to relevant written laws, (d) ensure electrical wiring systems comply with safety requirements according to relevant written laws, (e) ensure employees receive necessary medical assistance, and (f) take preventive measures to contain infectious diseases as ordered by the Medical Officer of Health and provide immunization arrangements at employer's expense.

title_short: Appointment of person in charge of accommodation
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer or accommodation provider must appoint at least one person in charge of accommodation who will be responsible for employees' safety and well-being and management of accommodations and amenities. This person must: (a) ensure employees comply with disciplinary rules, (b) visit and inspect accommodation at least twice a month and keep inspection records as determined by the Director General, and (c) ensure an employee is taken to a clinic or hospital if the employee complains of health issues or appears unwell, and keep records of complaints as determined by the Director General.

title_short: Building endangering health or safety
legal_content_plain_en: The Director General shall cause to be inspected: (a) by a Medical Officer of Health, any building, estate hospital, group estate hospital or clinic which appears likely to endanger health due to its design, site, size, sanitation, water quality or other conditions; and (b) by the District Engineer, any building, estate hospital, group estate hospital or clinic which appears likely to endanger safety due to its construction, state of repair or condition. After inspection, officials shall submit reports with recommendations on necessary measures. The Director General may then order employers to demolish and replace, alter or repair buildings or make good deficiencies within specified time and conditions, and may direct that no employee or dependants occupy such buildings pending compliance.

title_short: General duties of employers
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer must ensure your safety, health and welfare at work by: providing safe equipment and work systems, ensuring safe handling of materials, giving you safety training and information, keeping the workplace safe with proper access routes, maintaining a safe working environment with adequate facilities, and having emergency procedures ready.

title_short: General duties of employers

title_short: General duties of employees at work
legal_content_plain_en: While at work, you must: take care of your own safety and others who might be affected by your actions, cooperate with your employer on safety requirements, wear protective equipment provided by your employer, and follow safety instructions. Breaking these rules can result in fines up to RM2,000 or jail time up to 3 months.

title_short: Duty of employer to formulate occupational safety and health policy
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer must prepare and regularly update a written safety and health policy statement and make sure all employees know about it and any changes to it.

title_short: Establishment of safety and health committee at place of work
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer must set up a safety and health committee if there are 40 or more workers at the workplace, or if ordered by the Director General. The employer must work with this committee to develop and check safety measures. Not following this can result in fines up to RM100,000 or jail time up to 1 year.

title_short: Accident reporting
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer must report any workplace accidents, dangerous incidents, occupational poisoning or diseases to the nearest occupational safety and health office. Medical practitioners must also report occupational diseases to the Director General.

title_short: Duty of employer to segregate employee suffering from infectious
legal_content_plain_en: If there is an infectious disease outbreak at your workplace, your employer must provide a place for you to be safely separated if directed by the Medical Officer of Health. Your employer must pay for your maintenance and treatment while you are segregated. If a Medical Officer believes you have an infectious disease or need to be removed for public health reasons, they can legally order you to be moved to a medical facility and kept there until you are discharged by written order from a Medical Officer.

title_short: Allotment of land
legal_content_plain_en: If you work and live at your workplace for at least 6 months, your employer must give you 250 square meters of land for growing food.

title_short: Community hall, sports and other recreational facilities
legal_content_plain_en: If there are 100 or more workers living at the workplace, your employer must build a community hall and provide sports and recreation facilities.

title_short: No rent or charge to be levied for benefits under this Part
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer cannot charge you rent or fees for housing, nursery, community hall, sports facilities, sanitation, or land allotment provided under this law.

title_short: Medical treatment in estate on which a hospital is not maintained
legal_content_plain_en: If there's no hospital available, your employer must establish and maintain a clinic for treating sick workers and their families, with a registered doctor visiting at least twice a month.

title_short: Weekly inspection of employees’ housing
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer must keep your housing area clean and sanitary, maintain proper drainage, collect refuse daily, and ensure bathrooms are clean - with weekly inspections by health officials.

title_short: Accommodation to be certified with Certificate for Accommodation
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer cannot provide accommodation without a Certificate for Accommodation - violating this can result in fines up to RM50,000.

title_short: Employer to give notice of occupation
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer must notify the Director General within 30 days when you occupy accommodation - failure to do so results in fines up to RM10,000.

title_short: Accommodation to comply with minimum standards
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer or accommodation provider must ensure that every accommodation provided for employees complies with the minimum standards required under this Act or any regulations made thereunder.

title_short: Deductions in respect of rent or charge for accommodation. Accommodation to comply with minimum standards
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer may collect rent or charges for accommodation provided, but this must be done through deductions from your wages according to conditions prescribed by the Minister.

title_short: Accommodation to comply with the laws of local authorities
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer or accommodation provider cannot use any building as accommodation if the building is unfit for human habitation according to relevant written laws. Violating this is an offence with fines up to RM50,000.

title_short: Accommodation to comply with the laws of local authorities
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer or accommodation provider cannot use any building as accommodation if the building is unfit for human habitation according to relevant written laws. Violating this is an offence with fines up to RM50,000.

title_short: Appointment of person in charge of accommodation
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer or accommodation provider must provide decent and adequate amenities in accordance with this Act or any regulations made thereunder.

title_short: Maintenance
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer and accommodation provider must ensure that every accommodation provided for employees is maintained as directed by the Director General.

title_short: Notice to vacate accommodation
legal_content_plain_en: If you resign or your employment is terminated with at least four weeks' notice, you must vacate the accommodation upon the effective date of termination. If your employment is terminated with less than four weeks' notice or with immediate effect, you must vacate the accommodation within four weeks from the date of notice or termination.

title_short: Employer not obligated to provide accommodation for employees’ dependants
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer is not obligated to provide accommodation for your dependants even if you are provided with accommodation under this Part.

title_short: Exemption
legal_content_plain_en: The Minister may by order exempt from all or any of the provisions of this Act any employer or class of employers or any building or class of buildings specified in the order.

title_short: Building to comply with requirements
legal_content_plain_en: No employer shall house or cause or permit to be housed any employee in any building which does not comply with the provisions of this Act or any regulations made thereunder. Buildings used for housing employees before this Act commenced may continue to be used if they comply with previous written laws, provided they are converted to comply with this Act. The Director General may permit existing buildings to continue being used subject to conditions and for periods he deems fit. If buildings do not comply after investigation, the Director General may order demolition, replacement, alteration, repair or making good of deficiencies with at least three months' notice.

title_short: Supply of water and electricity and maintenance of houses
legal_content_plain_en: Where employees and their dependants are provided with housing at their place of employment, it shall be the duty of the employer to: (a) provide free and adequate piped water drawn from a public main, or where permitted by the Director General, provide free and adequate supply of potable piped water from any other source filtered and treated as approved by the Director General; (b) provide adequate electricity supply; (c) ensure that the buildings are kept in a good state of repair and painted to present a satisfactory appearance; and (d) ensure that no unauthorized extensions or structural alterations are made to the buildings. The adequacy of water and electricity supply shall be determined by the Director General, who may approve alternative water supply methods or exempt employers from certain requirements if provision is not practicable or viable.

title_short: HOUSING AND OTHER AMENITIES
legal_content_plain_en: For any building to be erected or converted for housing of employees or for use as a nursery or community hall, plans of the building and its site must be submitted to the Director General for approval, and no work relating to the building shall begin until the plans have been approved. The approving authority shall be the Director General for building plans and the Medical Officer of Health for site plans and sanitary arrangements.

title_short: Building not originally built for the housing of employees
legal_content_plain_en: A building originally built for a purpose other than housing of employees shall not be used for or converted for the purpose of housing employees unless an application has been made to and approved by the Director General, accompanied by a plan of the site and building setting out conversion details.

title_short: Length of eligible period and entitlement to maternity allowance
legal_content_plain_en: Every female employee is entitled to maternity leave for at least 98 consecutive days (eligible period) for each confinement and to receive maternity allowance from her employer. To qualify for maternity allowance, you must have worked for at least 90 days during the 9 months before confinement and been employed at any time in the 4 months immediately before confinement. Maternity leave cannot start earlier than 30 days before confinement or later than the day after confinement, unless a medical officer certifies you cannot perform duties due to advanced pregnancy (then you can start up to 14 days earlier). You can return to work during maternity leave if certified fit by a registered medical practitioner with employer consent. You are not entitled to maternity allowance if you have 5 or more surviving children at the time of confinement.

title_short: Restriction on termination  of female employee after eligible period
legal_content_plain_en: If you remain absent from work after your eligible maternity period ends due to illness certified by a registered medical practitioner arising from pregnancy and confinement, and this makes you unfit for work, it is an offence for your employer to terminate your employment until 90 days after your eligible period expires.

title_short: Rest day
legal_content_plain_en: You are entitled to one full rest day each week as determined by your employer. For shift workers, any continuous period of at least 30 hours constitutes a rest day. Your employer must prepare a monthly roster showing appointed rest days and make it available for inspection. The Director General may permit employers to grant rest days on any day of the month instead of weekly with proper conditions. This does not apply during maternity leave, sick leave, or temporary disablement periods.

title_short: Work on rest day
legal_content_plain_en: You cannot be compelled to work on your rest day unless engaged in continuous work or shift work. If you work on a rest day: for daily/hourly workers - you get 1 day's wages at ordinary rate for work up to half normal hours, or 2 days' wages for work exceeding half but not exceeding normal hours; for monthly/weekly workers - you get wages equivalent to half ordinary rate for work up to half normal hours, or 1 day's wages for work exceeding half but not exceeding normal hours. Any work exceeding normal hours on rest days must be paid at double your hourly rate.

title_short: Holidays
legal_content_plain_en: You are entitled to paid holidays at your ordinary rate of pay for at least 11 public holidays per year, including 5 mandatory designated public holidays: National Day, Birthday of Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Birthday of Ruler or Yang di-Pertuan Negeri (depending on your work location), Workers' Day, and Malaysia Day. Your employer can designate the remaining 6 public holidays from other gazetted public holidays. If a public holiday falls on your rest day or another public holiday, the working day immediately following becomes a paid public holiday. Your employer must display a notice specifying the remaining gazetted public holidays at the workplace. If you work on a public holiday, you get additional compensation on top of your normal wages based on your pay structure.

title_short: Annual leave
legal_content_plain_en: You are entitled to paid annual leave of: 8 days for every 12 months if employed less than 2 years, 12 days for every 12 months if employed 2-5 years, or 16 days for every 12 months if employed 5+ years. If you haven't completed 12 months of service when your contract ends, your annual leave entitlement is calculated proportionally. Annual leave is in addition to rest days and public holidays. You can carry forward unused annual leave, but if you don't take leave for 12 consecutive months without permission, you lose entitlement to that leave.

title_short: Sick leave
legal_content_plain_en: After medical examination at employer's expense, you are entitled to paid sick leave of: 14 days per year if employed less than 2 years, 18 days per year if employed 2-5 years, 22 days per year if employed 5+ years, or 60 days per year if hospitalization is necessary. Sick leave must be certified by a registered medical practitioner or medical officer. If you take uncertified sick leave or fail to inform/attend your employer within 48 hours, you may be absent without permission and without pay.

title_short: Paternity leave
legal_content_plain_en: Married male employees are entitled to paid paternity leave at ordinary rate of pay for 7 consecutive days for each confinement, limited to 5 confinements regardless of number of spouses. To qualify, you must have worked for the same employer for at least 12 months before the leave starts and notify your employer of your spouse's pregnancy at least 30 days before expected confinement or as early as possible after birth.

title_short: Under Part IX
legal_content_plain_en: Your employer commits an offence if they: fail to grant maternity leave when you're entitled, fail to pay maternity allowance to you or your nominee/legal representative, fail to pay maternity allowance in the prescribed manner, or contravene maternity leave protection rules. If convicted, the court can order your employer to pay the maternity allowance you're entitled to in addition to any other penalties.
